questions.question: What is the sum of all prime numbers from 50 to 65?
What is the value of 2 + 4 + 6 + ……. 40?
questions.solution:
**Giv****en,**

2 + 4 + 6 + …….. + 40

**Fo****rmula:**

Sum of first n even number = n × (n + 1)

**Ca****lculation:**

Total even numbers between 2 to 40 = 20

Sum first 20 even numbers (2 + 4 + 6 + …… + 40)

⇒ 20 × (20 + 1)

⇒ 20 × 21

⇒ 420

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f8dca65909f9faba98a96111792ecf4bf8a69f70d4ef1419e1068565a712e35a.png] 

2 + 4 + 6 + ……. 40, numbers are in Ap with common difference 2.

Hence, 40 = 2 + (n – 1) × 2

⇒ 38 = 2(n - 1)

⇒ 19 = n – 1

⇒ n = 20

Now, sum of n terns in AP = N/2(1st term + last term)

= (20/2)(2 + 40)

= 10 × 42

= 420.

questions.question: What is the Least Common Multiple of 2/3, 4/7 and 12/35?
questions.solution:
**G****iven,**

The given fractions are 2/3, 4/7 and 12/35

**Form****ula:**

LCM of fractions = LCM of numerators/HCF of denominators

**Calcu****lation:**

2 = 2 × 1

4 = 2 × 2

12 = 2 × 2 × 3

LCM of 2, 4, 12 = 12

3 = 3 × 1

7 = 7 × 1

35 = 5 × 7 

HCF of 3, 7, 35 = 1

∴ Required LCM = 12/1

questions.question: Average age of a group of 20 boys is 15 years. If a boy leaves the group, then the average age becomes 14.5 years. What is the age (in years) of the boy who left the group?
questions.solution:
**Gi****ven,**

Average of a group of 20 boys = 15

If a boy leaves the group, then the average age of remaining boys = 14.5

**Fo****rmula:**

Average = Sum of all observations/Total number of all observations

**Cal****culation:**

Sum of age of 20 boys = 15 × 20 = 300

Sum of age of 19 boys = 14.5 × 19 = 275.5

∴ Age of the boy who left the group = 300 – 275.5 = 24.5 

__**Smart trick**__

Required age of boy = New average + Difference in averages × Number of boys 

= 14.5 + (15 - 14.5) × 20 

= 14.5 + 0.5 × 20 

= 14.5 + 10 

= 24.5.

questions.question: The profit earned by selling an article for 900 is equal to the loss incurred by selling the same article for 500. What should be the selling price (in Rs.) of the article to earn a profit of 30%
questions.solution:
**Formula:**

Profit = SP – CP

Loss = CP - SP

**Calculation:**

Let cost price of the article be Rs. x, then

According to the questions

900 – x = x – 500

⇒ x + x = 900 + 500

⇒ 2x = 1400

⇒ x = 1400/2

⇒ x = 700

∴ Cost price of the article = Rs. 700

∴ Selling price of the article = 700 × (130/100) = Rs. 910

questions.question: What will be the net discount (in %) on giving two successive discounts of 30% and 10%?
questions.solution:
**Formula:**

If percentage discount of two successive discount x% and y%, then

Single equivalent discount = x + y – (xy/100)

**Calculation:**

**Short Trick:**

Single discount of two successive discount of 30% and 10% = 30 + 10 – [(30 × 10)/100] = 40 – 3 = 37%

**Detailed Method:**

Let MP of an article be Rs. 100

SP of the article after two successive discount of 30% and 10% = 100 × (70/100) × (90/100) = Rs. 63

Net discount = 100 – 63 = 37

∴ Net discount % = (37/100) × 100 = 37%

questions.question: The breadth of a rectangular hall is 4/5 of its length. If the area of the floor is 500 m², then what is the difference (in metres) between the length and breadth of the hall?
questions.solution:
**Given,**

Area of the floor of rectangular hall = 500 m²

**Formula:**

Area of the rectangle = length × breadth

**Calculation:**

Let length of the rectangular hall be 5x

Breadth of the rectangular hall = 5x × (4/5) = 4x

According to the question

5x × 4x = 500

⇒ 20x² = 500

⇒ x² = 500/20

⇒ x² = 25

⇒ x = 5

Difference between length and breadth = 5x – 4x = x = 5

questions.question: A car travels at a speed of 100 km/hr and covers a particular distance in 2 hour 30 minutes. Another car travelling at the speed of 60 km/hr will cover the same distance in how much time (in hours)?
P and Q have invested in a business of 4 : 7. P has invested for 21 months. If P and Q receive profit in the ratio of 3 : 5, then for how many month did Q invested?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We know that, Profit Ratio = Ratio of Equivalent Capital (Investment × Time).

Profit of P / Profit of Q = (P's Capital × P's Time) / (Q's Capital × Q's Time)

3 / 5 = (4 × 21) / (7 × Q's Time)

3 / 5 = 12 / Q's Time ⇒ Q's Time = (12 × 5) / 3 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20 months.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Investment ratio of P : Q = 4 : 7

P's investment period = 21 months

Profit ratio of P : Q = 3 : 5

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ee0d711218b24c937aa363a8ab7bbcf8d9ba6b8b887c9dd2474c9b2fa212e0a6.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Profit Ratio = (Capital of A × Time of A) : (Capital of B × Time of B)

**Calculation:**

Let the investments of P and Q be 4x and 7x respectively.

Let Q's investment period be t months.

⇒ Profit of P / Profit of Q = (4x × 21) / (7x × t)

⇒ 3 / 5 = 84x / 7xt

⇒ 3 / 5 = 12 / t

⇒ 3 × t = 12 × 5

⇒ 3t = 60

⇒ t = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20 months.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Principle of Partnership

In a partnership, the profit is distributed in proportion to the product of capital invested and the time period of investment. Hence, Profit = Capital × Time.

Active and Sleeping Partners

An active partner actively manages the business and usually receives a fixed salary or a specific percentage of profit for their effort, while the remaining profit is distributed according to capital investments.

Joining Mid-Way

If a business runs for a specific period (e.g., 12 months) and a partner joins after 'x' months, their capital is considered invested only for the remaining time, i.e., (12 − x) months.

questions.question: Two taps P and R can fill a tank in 16 hours and 24 hours respectively while a third tap S can empty the same tank in 48 hours. If all three taps are opened together, then in how many hours the tank will be filled?
questions.solution:
**Given,**

P alone can fill the tank in 16 hrs

R alone can fill the tank in 24 hrs

S alone can empty the full tank in 48 hrs

Formula used:

For LCM method,

If a pipe fills a tank in 'a' hours and an another fills the same tank in 'b' hours and a third one empties the full tank in 'c' hours and all of them are opened together, then

Total work = LCM of the times taken by three different pipes = LCM of (a, b, c)

Efficiency of first pipe = LCM of (a, b, c)/a

Efficiency of second pipe = LCM of (a, b, c)/b

Efficiency of third pipe = LCM of (a, b, c)/c

Combined efficiency of them = (+ efficiency of 1st pipe) + (+ efficiency of 2nd pipe) + (- efficiency of 3rd pipe)

[(+ve) sign for the efficiency of the pipe which fills the tank and (-ve) sign for the efficiency of the pipe which empties the tank.]

Time taken to fill the tank = Total work/The combined efficiency of the pipes.

For Alternate method,

If a pipe fills a tank in 'a' hours and an another fills the same tank in 'b' hours and a third one empties the full tank in 'c' hours and all of them are opened together, the net part filled in 1 hour = 1/a + 1/b - 1/c

∴ Time taken to fill the tank = 1/(1/a + 1/b - 1/c) = abc/(bc + ac - ab) hours

**Calculation:**

Let total work = LCM of (16, 24 and 48) = 48 units

Efficiency of P = (+) 48/16 = (+) 3 units/day

Efficiency of R = (+) 48/24 = (+) 2 units/day

Efficiency of S = (-) 48/48 = (-) 1 unit/day

Combined efficiency = 3 + 2 - 1 = 4 units/day

**∴ Time taken to fill the tank if all three pipes opened together = 48/4 = 12 hours **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f72be33799c08d3322a2907949d25e7543e352bc7880a277f6efed7f62d7c04b.png] 

P fills in 16 hours

R fills in 24 hours

S empties in 48 hours

So required time to fill the tank = 1/(1/16 + 1/24 - 1/48) hours = 48/4 hours = 12 hours

**∴ Time taken to fill the tank is 12 hours.**
